name: Sort + fixed-size sliding window
space: O(1) extra (O(log n) for the sort)
whenToUse: The standard answer. Sorting costs O(n log n); the window pass after it is O(n).

card.signals: "pick the scores of any k students": the order of nums does not matter, so sorting is allowed. "highest and lowest" only depends on the two ends of a group, and "minimized" asks for the tightest group. After sorting, the tightest group of k scores is always k neighbours: a window of fixed size k.
card.pattern: sort first, then a fixed-size window of k cells slides from left to right. In a sorted window the lowest score is nums[left] and the highest is nums[right], so each window costs O(1).
card.coreIdea: for each window [left, right] with right − left + 1 = k, diff = nums[right] − nums[left]. Keep the smallest diff. No running sum is needed: only the two ends matter.

invariant: nums is sorted, the window nums[left..right] has exactly k scores, and smallest is the smallest diff of all windows checked so far.
